rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the six-compound elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing late peaks. A midpoint temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.
Injection 1 already achieved the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method while retaining injection 1 as the optimal-score fallback.

The 8-minute gradient retains full resolution with a minimum R of 3.24. Shorten by another grid step at fixed temperature to reduce analysis time and measure the critical pair’s response to gradient steepness.
The critical pair remains comfortably resolved at R = 2.46. Test a 4-minute gradient with all other settings fixed to seek a faster method that preserves the maximum CRF.

Test the shortest allowed gradient to locate the speed–resolution boundary. The first pair is likely to fall below R = 1.5; if so, the 4-minute method remains the fastest fully resolved method tested.

Only the first pair fails at the shortest gradient. Test higher temperature at the same slope to determine whether temperature-driven selectivity can recover its resolution while further shortening retention; retain injection 4 as the fully resolved fallback.

Heating worsened the critical separations, so test the lowest temperature at the same gradient to establish the opposite selectivity limit. This will show how much additional slope reduction is needed to recover full resolution in a short method.

Reduce gradient steepness at the temperature giving the best short-gradient selectivity, aiming to raise the critical pair from R = 1.23 to at least 1.5. The last compound will likely elute during the final hold, so monitor its retention against the 10-minute scoring threshold.

Shift the successful 0.70-wide gradient window upward while keeping its slope and temperature fixed, aiming to accelerate the late peak without sacrificing the critical separation. Check whether the higher starting organic fraction compresses the early pair too much.

Raise the starting organic fraction by one grid step to shorten late-peak retention while making the gradient slightly shallower. Monitor the early pair for loss of retention; injection 9 remains the fastest fully resolved method tested.

Use the early pair’s resolution margin to test a 5 °C temperature increase, seeking shorter retention with CRF still at 1.000. Keep the gradient fixed to isolate the temperature effect near the fastest fully resolved method.

Test whether a slightly higher starting organic fraction can further shorten the run while the shallower gradient preserves resolution. The main risk is compression of the early pair near the dead time; injection 11 remains the fastest fully resolved fallback.

Return to the starting fraction that preserved early retention and test one more temperature step to locate the speed–resolution boundary. The first pair may drop below R = 1.5; injection 11 remains the fastest fully resolved method tested.

Narrow the gradient at 35 °C to test whether reduced steepness restores the first pair to R ≥ 1.5. The lower endpoint may delay the last peak during the hold, so compare both resolution and retention with injection 11.

Lower the starting organic fraction to retain the early pair beyond the gradient arrival, where slope adjustment can better improve separation. This tests whether full resolution can be recovered at 35 °C without lengthening the programmed gradient.

Reduce the endpoint by one grid step to make the gradient shallower, aiming to lift the critical pair from R = 1.42 above 1.5. This should recover maximum CRF at 35 °C, although the final hold will likely make it slower than injection 11.

Return to the fastest fully resolved temperature and starting fraction, then lower the endpoint one step to test a modest resolution-margin improvement. Injection 16 is borderline despite its rounded CRF, so injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Lower the starting organic fraction one step from injection 17 to move the first peak farther from the unretained region while testing whether full resolution survives. This explores an alternative maximum-score method; injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved choice.

Lower temperature one step from injection 18 to improve the critical pair’s narrow resolution margin while keeping the early peaks retained. This tests a more robust maximum-score alternative; injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Raise the starting fraction one step from injection 19 to shorten retention and test whether the shallower gradient improves the critical pair’s resolution margin. This refines a fully resolved alternative near injection 11, which remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test whether cooling to 25 °C rescues the early-pair compression observed at this starting fraction at 30 °C. This completes the nearby starting-fraction boundary check; injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Return to a starting fraction that retains the early pair and reduce the endpoint one step from injection 19 to increase its resolution margin. The maximum CRF is already secured; this tests a less borderline alternative while retaining injection 11 as the fastest fully resolved method.

Raise temperature one step from injection 22 to shorten the final hold while using some of the critical pair’s resolution margin. This should provide another fully resolved method with better early retention than injection 11, which remains the fastest confirmed choice.

Raise the starting fraction one step from injection 23 to shorten retention while testing whether the shallower gradient preserves full resolution. This refines the maximum-score region without repeating a method; injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved choice.

Use the final injection to test a larger critical-pair resolution margin by cooling injection 24 one temperature step, with elution still expected well within 10 minutes. The maximum CRF is already achieved, and injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.
